$comment: The five events the brief requires, defined before any of them is collected. A field that no source populates stays absent; it is never defaulted to zero in a report.

design_constraints.host: GitHub Pages serves static files only - there is no server to receive an event here.
design_constraints.chosen_shape: client-side recorder + an optional self-hosted collector (scripts/collect.mjs). Endpoint unset = events buffered locally only, and the site says so.
privacy: no IP capture server-side (only the access log the host keeps anyway)
session token is random, stored in sessionStorage, and dies with the tab
no page text, no form contents, and no referrer beyond the origin is sent

events.definition: A reader loaded a page on this site.
events.why_this_and_not_more: Path plus a timestamp answers 'did anyone arrive', which is the question Search Console only answers for impressions. Deliberately excludes scroll, mouse and timing so the payload stays explainable in one sentence.

events.definition: A reader loaded a guide, tagged with its slug and cluster.
events.why_this_and_not_more: Lets topic demand be read per guide without a separate scroll-tracking layer. Distinguishable from page_view because the guide set is the editorial bet being tested.
events.conversion_role: input to 'which topic earned the click'

events.definition: A reader clicked a sponsored commerce link.
events.why_this_and_not_more: This is the only event with direct revenue meaning. 'placement' (card | guide-inline | cluster | compare-row) makes it possible to say which surface earns, which is the entire point of measuring before optimising.
events.conversion_role: numerator for click-through; the join key to Amazon's click report
events.privacy_note: records our own product id and the link's placement, never the destination URL's query string

events.definition: A reader asked the page to copy a validated Special Link - an explicit, deliberate buying action.
events.trigger: click on the 'copy link' control on a product page
events.why_this_and_not_more: Higher-intent than a click on a card and it survives ad-blocking of outbound navigation. It is also the event that ties a reader action back to the product-intent record (register/products.json) the brief requires.
events.conversion_role: leading indicator when clicks are under-counted
events.privacy_note: clipboard action only; nothing read from the clipboard

events.definition: A reader opened a page whose register row is unverified or unresolved, i.e. we showed them a blank where a number should be.
events.trigger: page_view on a page carrying a data-gap notice, with the flag id
events.why_this_and_not_more: The brief wants the missing-information list to be actionable. If readers never look at the gap, closing it is low priority; if they crowd it, that is the strongest possible signal that prices or ratings are worth the API spend. Measuring our own holes turns FLG rows into a ranked backlog.
events.conversion_role: modifier - reads alongside click-through to show whether withheld data is costing revenue

explicitly_not_instrumented: scroll depth and dwell time - noisy, low decision value, high creep factor
mouse movement or any fingerprinting input
third-party pixels of any kind, including ad-network tags
recording what the reader typed into on-site search (the zero-result count is aggregated instead)

conversion_reporting.rule: Orders, units and earnings come only from Associates Central reports into register/ledger.json. This event stream never asserts a sale happened, because a click is the last thing this site can actually observe.
conversion_reporting.why: Attribution belongs to Amazon's session cookie. Any conversion figure computed here would be a guess wearing a decimal point.

collector_contract.response: 204 on accept, 400 on unknown event id
collector_contract.totals: GET /summary returns per-event counts per day
collector_contract.configured_by: window.SHOPNOW_COLLECTOR (string URL) injected by the builder only when register/site.json carries a collector_url
